calculation.intro: Upload a 5-section division data file (corners; H/V orientation; owners + percentages; road corner SW/NW/SE/NE; road width). The tool computes where the border between each owner must be — carving out a shared road strip along one long side, then dividing the remaining land by each owner's ownership fraction — and lets you review the result on the map before creating the properties and a group.

importance.title: Importance
importance.note: Reflects the subjective value you assign to this item, regardless of time or context. No justification is needed — this is your personal assessment.
importance.statementLow: This item is currently considered to have LOW importance — it is kept for reference but is not a priority.
importance.statementMedium: This item is currently considered to have MEDIUM importance — it is relevant and worth tracking.
importance.statementHigh: This item is currently considered to have HIGH importance — it is a priority and must be kept up to date.

relevance.title: Relevance
relevance.note: Indicates where this item stands on the time axis. An item can be obsolete or historical yet still carry high importance (e.g. a historical deed).
relevance.statementInactive: This item is INACTIVE — it was once relevant but is no longer applicable. It is kept for audit purposes only.
relevance.statementHistorical: This item is HISTORICAL — it belongs to the past and retains documentary or legal significance even though it is no longer in effect.
relevance.statementCurrent: This item is CURRENT — it is actively in use and reflects the present situation.
relevance.statementFuture: This item has FUTURE relevance — it is anticipated to become significant or active at a later date.

provenance.title: Provenience
provenance.note: Records how this item entered the system. Each change is logged in the history below with the date it was recorded.
provenance.statementManual: This item was entered manually using the Add new button — all data was typed in directly by a user.
provenance.statementImage: This item was created from a graphics file (a scan or a photo). The image is stored as-is — the nickname was taken from the filename and the code was auto-assigned. No content was extracted from the image.
provenance.statementDocFile: This item was created from a PDF, Word or plain-text file. The file is stored as-is; no content was extracted from it automatically.
provenance.statementCoordinateFile: This item was created from a cadastral coordinate file (.txt) — the Stereo 70 corner coordinates were read from the file and used to build the geometry.
provenance.statementAlgorithm: This item was generated automatically by an algorithm (e.g. polygon division or geometric computation).
provenance.statementAiInterpreted: This item was interpreted by an AI model from an image or document via a cloud API — the result should be reviewed by a person.
provenance.statementExternalFeed: This item arrived from an external system or data feed — verify the source and accuracy of the data.
provenance.algorithmNotFound: Source calculation not found (may have been deleted).

STR-01.requirement: The folder you choose contains only folders: one per property, plus common and floating if you need them. No file sits directly in it.
STR-01.example: Correct: 47per2-225per3per24, 48-50D, common. Wrong: a file contract.pdf placed directly in the chosen folder.
STR-01.violation: The chosen folder contains {files, plural, one {one file that is not inside a folder} other {# files that are not inside a folder}}: {examples}. Move each file into the property folder it belongs to, into common, or into floating.

STR-02.requirement: The chosen folder holds at most {max} properties. common and floating do not count.
STR-02.example: Correct: {max} property folders, plus common and floating. Wrong: one more property folder beyond those.
STR-02.violation: The chosen folder holds {found, plural, one {one property} other {# properties}}, and the limit is {max}. More than that at once is hard to keep track of. Make a second folder and split the properties between them; if you have shared documents, put a copy of the common folder in each.

STR-03.requirement: No two folders in the chosen folder may mean the same property.
STR-03.example: Correct: one folder per property. Wrong: 47per2-225per3 next to 47PER2-225per3||acte vechi — the same tarla and parcela, spelled differently.
STR-03.violation: The folders {folder} and {other} mean the same property ({identity}). Keep a single folder for it and move the documents from the other one into it.

STR-04.requirement: Every folder in the chosen folder is either a property, or common, or floating. A property name starts with the tarla and the parcela separated by a hyphen. per stands in for the slash, which cannot be used in a folder name.
STR-04.violation: The folder {folder} is neither a property, nor common, nor floating. Rename it with the tarla and the parcela, for example 47per2-225per3per24, or move the files out of it into common or floating and delete the empty folder.

STR-05.requirement: The shared folders are named exactly common and floating, in lower case.
STR-05.example: Correct: common, floating. Wrong: Common, COMMON, Floating.
STR-05.violation: The folder {folder} looks like {expected} but is not spelled the same way. Rename it to exactly {expected}, in lower case.

STR-06.requirement: If you add a description after the tarla and the parcela, separate it with two vertical bars: ||.
STR-06.violation: The name {folder} carries extra text after the tarla and the parcela but does not separate it with ||. Rename the folder to {suggestion}.

STR-07.requirement: The files sitting directly in a property folder — or in common or floating — cannot all be numbered scans. The pages of a scanned document live in a subfolder whose name is the document title.
STR-07.violation: Every file sitting directly in {folder} is a numbered scan ({files, plural, one {one file} other {# files}}). A number is not a document title, so the import would fall back on the folder name, or on the numbers themselves. Move them into a subfolder whose name is the document title.

STR-08.requirement: A property has at most one coordinate file: its name starts with coord and its extension is .txt. Having none is allowed and creates a property with no outline.
STR-08.example: Correct: coord 47per2-225per3per24.txt, alone in the property folder. Wrong: coord 47per2.txt and coord vechi.txt in the same folder.
STR-08.violation: The property {folder} contains {found, plural, one {one coordinate file} other {# coordinate files}}: {examples}. At most one is allowed. Keep only the correct one and take the rest out of the property folder.

STR-09.requirement: The common and floating folders contain no coordinate files. Coordinates belong to a single property.
STR-09.example: Correct: coord 47per2-225per3per24.txt in the property folder. Wrong: the same file placed in common.
STR-09.violation: The folder {folder} contains {found, plural, one {one coordinate file} other {# coordinate files}}: {examples}. Move each coordinate file into the property folder it refers to.

STR-10.requirement: A page folder contains only files. It has no further folders inside it.
STR-10.example: Correct: 47per2-225per3per24 > Contract vanzare > 1.jpg, 2.jpg. Wrong: 47per2-225per3per24 > Contract vanzare > Anexe > 1.jpg.
STR-10.violation: The page folder {folder} contains {subfolders, plural, one {one more folder} other {# more folders}}: {examples}. A page folder cannot have folders inside it. Move each of them one level up, beside this folder.

STR-11.requirement: Every page folder contains at least one file.
STR-11.example: Correct: Contract vanzare holding 1.jpg and 2.jpg. Wrong: Contract vanzare, empty.
STR-11.violation: The folder {folder} is empty. Delete it, or put the pages of the document into it.

STR-12.requirement: Inside a page folder every file is a scan whose name is just a number. The folder name becomes the document title.
STR-12.example: Correct: 1.jpg, 2.jpg, 3.jpg. Wrong: CVC 1 pg 1.jpg, scan final.jpg, 1.pdf.
STR-12.violation: In the page folder {folder}, {offending, plural, one {one file is not a numbered scan} other {# files are not numbered scans}}: {examples}. Rename each such file to a number — 1, 2, 3… — or take it out of this folder; otherwise each page becomes a separate document.

STR-13.requirement: Inside a page folder no two files may carry the same number.
STR-13.example: Correct: 1.jpg, 2.jpg. Wrong: 1.jpg and 01.jpg, which are both page 1.
STR-13.violation: In {folder} several files carry page number {number}: {examples}. The page order would be arbitrary. Renumber them so each number appears exactly once.

STR-14.requirement: Pages are numbered 1, 2, 3… with no gaps.
STR-14.example: Correct: 1.jpg, 2.jpg, 3.jpg. Wrong: 1.jpg, 3.jpg, 4.jpg, or 5449.jpg and 31316.jpg, which are scanner counters rather than page numbers.
STR-14.violation: The folder {folder} holds {pages, plural, one {one page numbered} other {# pages numbered}} from {lowest} to {highest}. Pages are numbered 1, 2, 3… with no gaps. Renumber the files in this folder starting from 1.

structure.title: Folder structure
structure.intro: Before the import, the folder on your computer has to look a certain way. Read the rules below, tick that you follow them, then choose the folder. The system checks it immediately and tells you exactly what needs putting right.

scope.topLevelFolder: The folders inside it: properties, “common” and “floating”
scope.pageFolder: The folders holding a document's pages

structure.acknowledgeHint: Tick once you have read the rules, and again after each correction you make in File Explorer. The tick is asked for on every check.
structure.violationsTitle: {count, plural, one {One thing to put right} other {# things to put right}}
structure.fixInstructions: Open the folder in File Explorer and make the corrections above — the system never touches your files. When you are done, come back here, tick again and press “Check again”.

truncated.title: The folder could not be read in full
truncated.intro: The check stopped before it had been through the whole folder, so we cannot say it is correct. Put the following right and check again.
truncated.depth: The check stopped: {count, plural, one {one folder is nested too deeply in the chosen folder} other {# folders are nested too deeply in the chosen folder}}. This is usually a shortcut pointing at a folder above it, which sends the check round in a circle. Delete the shortcut or move it out of the chosen folder. Examples:
truncated.budget: The chosen folder holds too many folders. The check stopped, and {count, plural, one {one folder was left unread} other {# folders were left unread}}. Split the properties across several folders and choose them one at a time. Examples of unread folders:
truncated.breadth: The chosen folder holds too many files. The check stopped, and {count, plural, one {one folder was not read to the end} other {# folders were not read to the end}}. Split the properties across several folders and choose them one at a time. Examples:

save.button: Save the rules as a page
save.hint: Downloads a page you can open or print while you work in File Explorer. It holds the rules and, if a folder has been checked, the complete list of what needs putting right.
save.notCheckedYet: No folder has been checked yet — this page holds the rules only.
save.warningsTitle: The folder could not be read in full
save.blocked: No structure rule was broken in the part that could be read, but the folder still cannot be imported — see below for why.

CON-01.requirement: A table saved as a .csv file cannot be imported: it is a set of data, not a document. Ordinary Excel files are imported and kept as they are.
CON-01.example: Right: the parcel schedule saved as “parcel schedule.pdf” or as “parcel schedule.xlsx”. Wrong: the same schedule saved as “parcel schedule.csv”.
CON-01.violation: {files, plural, one {One file in the folder is a .csv table and cannot be imported. Save it as a PDF from the program that produced it and delete the old file, or take it out of the chosen folder.} other {# files in the folder are .csv tables and cannot be imported. Save them as PDFs from the programs that produced them and delete the old files, or take them out of the chosen folder.}}

CON-02.requirement: Photographs taken on an iPhone are saved in a format the system can neither display nor read. They upload, but what is left in the archive is pages nobody can open.
CON-02.example: Right: “Ionescu ID card.jpg”. Wrong: “IMG_0421.heic”, the photo copied straight off the phone.
CON-02.violation: {files, plural, one {One file is a photograph taken on an iPhone, in a format the system cannot open. Copy the photo across from the phone again as an ordinary photograph ending in .jpg and delete the old file, or take it out of the chosen folder.} other {# files are photographs taken on an iPhone, in a format the system cannot open. Copy the photos across from the phone again as ordinary photographs ending in .jpg and delete the old files, or take them out of the chosen folder.}}

CON-03.requirement: A file the system does not recognise stops the whole import: it halts and asks you about each such file in turn before anything is imported. Scanned deeds, photographs, PDFs, Word and Excel documents, and text files are imported.
CON-03.example: Right: “sale contract.pdf”, “sketch.jpg”, “notes.txt”. Wrong: “project.xyz”, or a file whose name has no ending at all, such as “scan1”.
CON-03.violation: {files, plural, one {The system does not recognise one file in the folder. The import would stop and ask you about it before importing anything else. Save it as a PDF or as a photograph and delete the old file, or take it out of the chosen folder.} other {The system does not recognise # files in the folder. The import would stop and ask you about each of them before importing anything else. Save them as PDFs or as photographs and delete the old files, or take them out of the chosen folder.}}

CON-04.requirement: Every file has to contain something. An empty file is usually a scan that was never finished saving.
CON-04.example: Right: “1.jpg”, which File Explorer shows under View → Details as a few hundred KB. Wrong: “1.jpg” which File Explorer shows as 0 KB.
CON-04.violation: {files, plural, one {One file in the folder is empty. Scan the document again and put the new file in its place, or take it out of the chosen folder.} other {# files in the folder are empty. Scan the documents again and put the new files in their place, or take them out of the chosen folder.}}

CON-05.requirement: A file cannot be larger than {limitMb} MB. In File Explorer choose View → Details: the Size column shows KB, and a thousand KB is one MB.
CON-05.example: Right: a page scanned at 200 dpi, a few hundred KB. Wrong: the same page scanned at maximum resolution, over {limitMb} MB.
CON-05.violation: {files, plural, one {One file in the folder is larger than {limitMb} MB and would fail to upload. Scan it again at a lower resolution, or split it into several files, then put what comes out in its place — or take it out of the chosen folder.} other {# files in the folder are larger than {limitMb} MB and would fail to upload. Scan them again at a lower resolution, or split them into several files, then put what comes out in their place — or take them out of the chosen folder.}}

CON-06.requirement: A scan may not be called “folder.jpg”. Windows uses that name for the picture shown on a folder's icon, so the import passes over it and the scan would be lost without a trace. The small pictures Windows makes by itself are not a problem — the system speaks up only when a “folder.jpg” is large enough to be a real scan.
CON-06.violation: {files, plural, one {One file is called “folder.jpg” and is too large to be just the icon picture — it looks like a real scan, and the import would not take it. Rename it: if it sits in a folder holding the pages of one document, give it the next page number; otherwise name it after the document. Or take the file out of the chosen folder.} other {# files are called “folder.jpg” and are too large to be just the icon picture — they look like real scans, and the import would not take them. Rename each one: if it sits in a folder holding the pages of one document, give it the next page number; otherwise name it after the document. Or take the files out of the chosen folder.}}

constraints.title: File constraints
constraints.intro: The folder's structure is correct. A check follows: every file in it has to be something the system can take in. Read what can and cannot be imported below, tick that you have taken note, then press “Check the files” — the same folder is checked, you do not have to choose it again.
constraints.rulesTitle: What the files have to satisfy

scope.fileType: What kinds of file can be imported
scope.fileSize: How large a file may be

constraints.acknowledge: I have read the file constraints
constraints.acknowledgeHint: Tick once you have read the constraints, and again after each correction you make in File Explorer. The tick is asked for on every check.
constraints.clean: Every file in the folder can be imported.
constraints.violationsTitle: {count, plural, one {One thing to put right} other {# things to put right}}
constraints.fixInstructions: Make the corrections above — the ones that are a move, a rename or a deletion you can make directly in File Explorer, and the system does not touch your files. If the file you took out was one page of a scanned document, renumber the remaining pages from 1. When you are done, come back here, tick again and press “Check again”.

unreadable.title: Files that could not be read
unreadable.intro: {count, plural, one {One file could not be opened, so we cannot say whether it satisfies the constraints. Usually the file is open in another program, the folder has been moved, or the drive is no longer connected. Close the program using it, make sure the folder is where it was, and check again. If it still cannot be read, take it out of the chosen folder.} other {# files could not be opened, so we cannot say whether they satisfy the constraints. Usually the files are open in another program, the folder has been moved, or the drive is no longer connected. Close the programs using them, make sure the folder is where it was, and check again. If they still cannot be read, take them out of the chosen folder.}}

save.button: Save the constraints as a page
save.hint: Downloads a page you can open or print while working in File Explorer. It holds the constraints and, once the files have been checked, the complete list of things to put right.
save.allClear: Every file in the folder can be imported.
save.blocked: No constraint was broken by the files that could be read, but the folder still cannot be imported — see below for why.
save.notCheckedYet: The files have not been checked yet — this page holds the constraints only.
save.warningsTitle: Files that could not be read

DUP-01.requirement: The same file must not sit in the chosen folder more than once. The system recognises copies by name and by size, looking past the ending Windows adds when you copy a file, such as “ - Copy”. Files whose name is nothing but a number are treated as scanned pages and are not compared with each other: a page cannot be taken out of a document without breaking its numbering. Documents scanned into page folders are compared whole, under the next rule; pages left directly in the property's folder are not checked at all.
DUP-01.example: Wrong: “contract vanzare.pdf” and “contract vanzare - Copy.pdf” both sit in the property's folder. Right: the file sits in one place only, and the copy has been taken out of the chosen folder.
DUP-01.violation: {sets, plural, one {One file sits in the chosen folder more than once} other {# files sit in the chosen folder more than once}}, {files, plural, one {one file} other {# files}} in total. Look at each group below: if they really are the same file, keep the one in the right place and take the others out of the chosen folder. If they are different documents, rename one of them so they no longer look alike. If you cannot tell, take them all out of the chosen folder — you can import them later.

DUP-02.requirement: The same document must not sit in more than one page folder inside the chosen folder. The system compares the pages: two folders holding exactly the same pages are very probably one and the same document, copied — even when the folders are named differently. Where the pages alone are not enough — a folder with a single page, or several pages of one size — the folders are only reported when one of them is marked as a copy and sits beside the other.
DUP-02.example: Wrong: “Contract vanzare” and “Contract vanzare - Copy” hold the same scanned pages. Right: the document sits in one page folder only, and the copy has been taken out of the chosen folder.
DUP-02.violation: {sets, plural, one {One document sits in more than one page folder} other {# documents sit in more than one page folder}}, {folders, plural, one {one folder} other {# folders}} in total. Open the folders below and compare the pages: if they are the same, keep one folder and take the others out of the chosen folder. If they are different documents, rename one of the folders so they no longer look alike. If you cannot tell, take them all out of the chosen folder — you can import them later.

duplication.title: Copies inside the chosen folder
duplication.intro: The structure and the files are in order. A check follows, on the same folder: nothing must sit in it twice, or it reaches the archive twice as well. Only the files in the chosen folder are compared, against each other — what is already in the system is checked at the next step.
duplication.acknowledge: I have read what counts as a copy
duplication.acknowledgeHint: Tick this after reading the explanations, and again after each correction made in File Explorer. The tick is asked for at every check.
duplication.clean: Nothing sits in the chosen folder twice.
duplication.violationsTitle: {count, plural, one {One thing to put right} other {# things to put right}}
duplication.fixInstructions: Open the folder in File Explorer and take the copies out of it — the system does not touch your files and never deletes anything itself. Do not delete anything before looking at the files: the system says two files look alike, not that they are. When you are done, tick below and press “Check again”.

group.name: {count, plural, one {One file} other {# files}}, one of them “{name}”
group.pages: {count, plural, one {One folder} other {# folders}}, {pages, plural, one {holding the same page} other {holding the same # pages}}

unsized.title: Files that could not be measured
unsized.intro: {count, plural, one {One file could not be measured, so we cannot say whether it sits in the folder a second time. Usually the file is open in another program, or the folder has been moved in the meantime. Close the program using it and check again, or take it out of the chosen folder.} other {# files could not be measured, so we cannot say whether they sit in the folder a second time. Usually the files are open in other programs, or the folder has been moved in the meantime. Close the programs using them and check again, or take them out of the chosen folder.}}

save.button: Save the list as a page
save.hint: Downloads a page you can open or print while you work in File Explorer. It holds the explanations and every copy found, with nothing left out.
save.allClear: Nothing sits in the chosen folder twice.
save.blocked: Nothing was found twice among the files that could be measured, but the folder still cannot be imported — see below for why.
save.notCheckedYet: The folder has not been checked yet — this page holds the explanations only.
save.warningsTitle: Files that could not be measured

PEX-01.explanation: A document in the chosen folder counts as already in the system when the archive holds a document with the same name and exactly the same files — the same file names and the same sizes. For a page folder every page is compared, not just the first. If you have since renamed the document in the system, or renumbered the pages in the folder, the system no longer recognises it and will import it again.
PEX-01.example: Right: “Contract vanzare.pdf” in the property's folder is 240 KB, and the archive already holds a document “Contract vanzare.pdf” with a single 240 KB file — it is the same document and is not imported a second time. Otherwise: if the archived document has a different name or a different size, it is treated as a new document.

PEX-02.explanation: A document that is already in the system is not imported a second time. If the file sits in a property folder in this import, the archived document is linked to that property instead, so you will find the property with the document attached and no second copy anywhere. If the file belongs to no property in this import, nothing happens to it at all.
PEX-02.example: A land-registry extract imported last year now sits in the folder for property 48-50: no second document is created, and the extract that already exists is linked to property 48-50.

PEX-03.explanation: Identity cards are imported again even when they appear to be here already. The reason is deliberate: the one in the system may have expired, and two copies of the same person are less serious than a person missing altogether. The system recognises an identity card by its file name, so make a note of these files and check the people after the import has finished.
PEX-03.example: “Buletin Ionescu.jpg” appears to be here already, but it is imported anyway. After the import, open the person Ionescu and see whether the details are the ones on the new card.

PEX-04.explanation: Coordinate files are imported again even when they appear to be here already. A property's corners have to show which document they were read from, and that document is created by this import — had the file been skipped, the new property would be left with corners and no source.
PEX-04.example: “coord 48-50.txt” has been imported once before, but it is imported again because the corners of property 48-50 in this import are made from it.

link.title: {count, plural, one {One existing document will be linked, not imported again} other {# existing documents will be linked, not imported again}}
link.intro: These files are already in the archive, so they are not imported again. The documents that already exist will be linked to the properties in this import — the ones named beside each row — so you will find them on the property's page.

skip.title: {count, plural, one {One document will not be imported again} other {# documents will not be imported again}}
skip.intro: These files are already in the archive and belong to no property in this import, so nothing happens to them. The archived documents are left untouched.

id-card.title: {count, plural, one {One identity card will be imported anyway} other {# identity cards will be imported anyway}}
id-card.intro: These files appear to be in the system already, but they are imported anyway because they look like identity cards: the one in the system may have expired, and it is better to have the person twice than not at all. Make a note of the files below and check the people once the import has finished.

coordinates.title: {count, plural, one {One coordinate file will be imported anyway} other {# coordinate files will be imported anyway}}
coordinates.intro: These files appear to be in the system already, but they are imported anyway: the corners of the properties in this import are made from them, and those corners have to show which document they were read from.

preexisting.title: Documents already in the system
preexisting.intro: The structure, the files and the copies are all in order. This is the first check that looks in the archive rather than in the chosen folder: the system tells you which of the documents are already in it and what will happen to each of them, before any of them is sent for classification. There is nothing to put right here: read what is about to happen, tick below, and carry on.
preexisting.acknowledge: I have read what happens to documents that are already in the system
preexisting.acknowledgeHint: Tick this after reading the explanations, and again after each check. The tick is asked for every time.
preexisting.check: See what is already in the system
preexisting.reportTitle: {count, plural, one {One document is already in the system} other {# documents are already in the system}}
preexisting.nothingToFix: There is nothing for you to put right in File Explorer about any of the above. Do read the list, though: if an archived document is not the one you had in mind, rename the file in your folder and the system will import it as a new document. When you are happy, tick below and press “Continue”.

unchecked.title: Files that could not be checked
unchecked.intro: {count, plural, one {One file could not be measured, so we cannot say whether it is already in the system. It will be imported, and if it was already there you will end up with two copies — check it after the import. Usually the file is open in another program.} other {# files could not be measured, so we cannot say whether they are already in the system. They will be imported, and any that were already there will reach the archive a second time — check them after the import. Usually the files are open in other programs.}}

failed.title: We could not find out what is already in the system
failed.intro: The system got no answer from the archive, so we cannot say which of these documents are already there. Nothing is wrong with the chosen folder. Try again in a moment.

scanning.title: Scanning
scanning.intro: The documents from {folder} that are about to be imported are being sent, a few at a time, to work out what kind of document each is. Nothing goes into the archive at this step.
scanning.whatItReads: Only the first page of each document is sent — just enough to recognise its type. Files that cannot be read as an image, and files already in the system, are not sent at all.
scanning.whatItWrites: What is recognised appears in the table below as it arrives.
scanning.waitHint: Wait for it to finish. If you change your mind, use “Cancel import” in the bar above.

importRun.title: Import
importRun.intro: The scan has finished. Nothing has been saved from {folder} yet — the button below is the first one that writes to the archive.
importRun.introWithProperties: The scan has finished. The properties you have confirmed so far have already been created and stay in the archive; the documents in {folder} have not been imported yet.
importRun.introRunning: The import of {folder} is under way. Whatever has been written so far stays in the archive, even if you stop here.
importRun.introDone: The import of {folder} has finished. The documents and properties it created are in the archive.
importRun.doneNote: This import cannot be started again from here — it would create the documents a second time. Check the results in the documents and properties lists; for a different folder, choose it below and the import restarts at Structure.
importRun.stepProperty: You confirm this import's property (or properties). Each one is created before its documents.
importRun.stepTags: The tags are prepared, from the folder names. Tags help you search — they link documents to nothing.
importRun.stepFiles: {count, plural, =0 {No new document is created} one {One document is created, with its files} other {# documents are created, with their files}}.
importRun.stepInterpret: Each document is then read by AI, automatically — its fields fill themselves in. People found in the documents are shown to you at the end, one at a time, for you to confirm; nobody is created without your confirmation.
importRun.costNote: AI reading costs money: {count, plural, =0 {no document will be read} one {at most one document will be read} other {at most # documents will be read}}.
importRun.writesNote: Documents already in the system were settled at the “Already in the system” step and are not imported a second time.
importRun.nothingToImport: There are no files to import from this folder.

information.title: How the import works
information.lead: The import runs in steps — the ones above. At each step the system checks one thing and shows you exactly what it found.
information.stops: Several times it will stop and ask you to put something right in the folder on your computer: rename a folder, move a file, or delete a spare copy. When that happens, open the folder in File Explorer, make the change, then come back here and press the re-check button. This is not a fault — it is how the import is meant to work.
information.neverTouchesFiles: The system never touches your files. It does not move them, rename them or delete them. You are the only one who changes them, from File Explorer.
information.nothingSavedUntilTheEnd: Nothing goes into the archive until the Import step. Until then you can cancel at any time, and before it cancels you are told exactly what is left behind.

cancel.title: Cancel the import?
cancel.intro: Here is what happens if you cancel now:

consequence.documentsKept: Documents already imported stay in the archive. They are not deleted — if you do not want them, remove them from the documents list.
consequence.propertyKept: The properties created or used for this import stay in the system — they are not deleted.
consequence.savedReportKept: The last import report stays saved and you can reopen it from this page.
consequence.classificationStops: Automatic classification stops. The documents in progress right now will not be classified.
consequence.classificationAlreadyPaid: Whatever has been classified automatically so far is lost. If you start the import again, the same documents will be sent again.
consequence.folderForgotten: The chosen folder is forgotten. On a later import you will have to choose it again.
consequence.nothingClassifiedYet: No document has been sent for automatic classification yet, so nothing has been spent.
consequence.filesUntouched: The files on your computer are left untouched.

result.title: The import has finished
result.intro: Everything that could be done with the files in {folder} has been done. Here is what came of it.
result.invitation: Please check the imported data: open a few properties and a few documents and confirm they are what you expected. If something is not right, it is far easier to put right now.

infoPanel.title: Ce este o Ștampilă?
infoPanel.body1: O ștampilă definește o caracteristică pe termen lung sau permanentă a obiectelor — persoane, proprietăți sau documente, indiferent de tip. De exemplu, o inițiativă de doi ani care implică multe persoane, proprietăți și documente primește o ștampilă specifică.
infoPanel.body2: Spre deosebire de grupuri, o ștampilă poate fi aplicată simultan pe orice combinație de tipuri de entități.
infoPanel.body3: Ștampilele pot descrie și calificatori subiectivi: nivelul de încredere ATT, potențialul unui obiect, prioritatea sau orice altă etichetă de evaluare personală. Este o practică recomandată să aplici cât mai multe ștampile și să creezi ștampile variate — aceasta adaugă valoare și bogăție utilizării datelor.
infoPanel.codeNote: Fiecare ștampilă primește un cod unic de trei litere (ex. STMP-AAA) atribuit automat.
infoPanel.seeAlso: Pentru acțiuni temporare pe un singur tip de obiect, folosește Grupuri.

infoPanel.title: Ce este un Grup?
infoPanel.body1: Un grup reunește elemente de un singur tip — proprietăți, persoane fizice, persoane juridice sau documente — pentru acțiuni și activități pe termen scurt. De exemplu: grupezi câteva proprietăți pentru o evaluare, câteva persoane pentru a le trimite un mesaj, sau câteva documente relevante pentru un eveniment cu o instituție.
infoPanel.body2: Elementele pot face parte din unul sau mai multe grupuri și pot fi eliminate oricând. Când un grup și-a îndeplinit misiunea, poate fi șters — elementele continuă să există independent.
infoPanel.codeNote: Fiecare grup primește un cod numeric unic (ex. GRP-001, GRP-002…) atribuit automat.
infoPanel.seeAlso: Pentru caracteristici pe termen lung sau permanente care se aplică pe mai multe tipuri de obiecte, folosește Ștampile.
